summary.headline: Somany Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 11.4% and FY26 to 9.3%; management guides at least 150 bps more margin improvement in FY27 despite gas-price shock.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 sales grew about 6% and FY26 about 5%, with EBITDA margin up in both periods (11.4% in Q4, 9.3% for FY26). Capacity utilisation was broadly flat at about 79% for the year, rising to 82% in Q4, and Somany Max reached near breakeven versus a loss of about INR 9 crore in Q4 FY25. Gas prices jumped from about 9 March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation, and Morbi capacity was disrupted, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity for organised players. Working capital improved sharply, with receivable days at 40 (from 51) and working capital lower by 4 days to 9 days. Management passed through about 16-17% tile price hikes and about 8% bathware and sanitaryware hikes, and said input cost increases are being fully recovered in retail but only about 85-90% in projects.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: GVT volumes up 3% while ceramic and PVT volumes fell 3%; average tile price increase of about 16-17% since March 2026. Company-wide utilisation around 79% for the year.

segments.name: Sanitaryware and bathware
segments.commentary: Sanitaryware grew 8% in FY26 to INR 320 crore; management targets double-digit growth in FY27. Bathware price hike of about 18% taken in February on brass costs, and a blended 8% hike in April. Only 25% of dealers currently stock sanitaryware.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Management expects healthy double-digit volume growth in FY27 for sanitaryware and adhesives combined; no separate adhesive figures were given.

segments.name: Outsourced / JV production
segments.commentary: Outsourced sales about 35-36% of volume after Acer and Amora moved from JV to outsourced status (about 30% excluding those). Total FY26 sales volume about 72 million sq m; capacity about 75 million sq m.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by at least 150 bps from the 9.3% FY26 base, to about 10.5-11% or better; management reiterated 10.8% or better when asked.
FY27 volume growth guided to decent single digits for tiles and double digits for sanitaryware and adhesives.
FY27 revenue growth of about 20-25% if current prices hold, per management, which would be driven by about 15% price hikes plus high single-digit volume growth; value outcome depends on gas prices.
Brand spend to rise slightly in absolute terms, while staying around 2% of sales as a percentage.
Capex limited to about INR 70-80 crore of routine capex and balancing equipment, mainly for the vintage plant and to add value at bathware plant.
South plant to move to a long-term gas contract from next month, expected to cut gas cost by at least INR 17-18 per SCM versus the current INR 78.
capex_capacity: Current gas price in Morbi is about INR 74 per SCM plus 6% (about INR 78) for May, sourced from GSPC; North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper.
Morbi restarting after gas supply from 1 May: about 60-65% of Morbi running in mid-May, with management expecting about 85% by month-end; labour shortage is the constraint.
Company plants running at about 100% of operating capacity across India, excluding a couple of kilns shut for product-mix reasons.
INR 30 crore invested in a new press at Somany Max to improve utilisation.
Vintage plant balancing equipment being added to turn it profitable; bathware capacity being augmented.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand improved in January and February with single-digit growth; March was disrupted as exports stalled. Industry exports were about INR 17,000+ crore versus about INR 18,000 crore potential.
April was a slow but growing month: Morbi supply shortfall, higher prices (company about 15-17%, Morbi about 30-35%), and dealer destocking caused slower volumes.
Gas cost increase is about INR 5.5-6 per sq ft; other input costs (transport, labour, packaging) add about INR 1-1.5 per sq ft; total cost pressure about INR 6.5-7 per sq ft.
Management says the price hike covers the full cost in retail, while about 15% of business (projects) recovers about 85-90%.
Sanitaryware and bathware blended price hike of about 8% in April 2026.
Stock levels at Q4 end reduced by about 2.5 million sq m (about 15 days) over the year; old stock over 180 days cleared in March.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are the receivable days and negative working capital, and what is the outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects receivable days to stay near current levels, possibly up 1-2 days. Working capital gains came from lower outsourced-vendor stock and clearance of old stock in March. Sustainability is uncertain given the delayed response to price hikes in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a tipping point where gas costs make running plants unviable?
qa_highlights.answer: Tile prices are about 15-20% below two years ago and current hikes bring prices back to historic levels. Management does not see plant shutdown even with a further 10-15% rise, excluding a severe oil shock (about USD 200/bbl).

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only about 2% in Q4 versus double digits for peers, and realisation lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume was focused on non-JV and outsourced material to clear inventory before April price increases. It said realisation was up INR 6 per sq m YoY, with the mix shifting toward cheaper outsourced product.

qa_highlights.question: Gas price differential between Morbi and North, and South plant pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi is about INR 74 plus 6% (about INR 78) per SCM for May; the North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper. South is INR 78 per SCM currently, but a long-term contract from next month should cut it by at least INR 17-18.

qa_highlights.question: Is the share buyback possible given the market leader's INR 300 crore buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for the next 6-8 months, due to an SEBI embargo tied to consolidation of wholly owned subsidiaries. Promoters bought shares before the trading window closed.

qa_highlights.question: Will Morbi's recovery affect outsourced volumes and FY27 supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced OEM plants for large organised players should keep running. Four or five supplier plants had short-term material gaps in April, expected to normalise in May. Full material availability is expected by June.

risks_watch: Gas prices and any further geopolitical escalation; management said price cuts would follow if gas prices fall.
Morbi restart pace (85% target by end-May) and labour availability; a 10-15% Morbi capacity may not restart.
Demand response to 15-17% tile price hikes; management expects pent-up demand but April was slow.
Transport and fuel costs, which had not yet been quantified after diesel and petrol price hikes.
Sustainability of working capital release and debtor days, and the 4-day rise in receivables risk.
Somany Max path to positive EBITDA in FY27, and Acer and Amora now sitting in the outsourced bucket.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins and industry structure, while openly cautious on near-term demand, gas costs and labour; management repeatedly tied its guidance to no further geopolitical shocks. Answers on gas pricing and April volumes were less precise and some figures were corrected or restated during Q&A.

So we are to gain from this disruption because a lot of the capacity in Morbi shut down, and everybody is now buying from the same source of gas.
Tile still being the most cheapest material for the flooring and wall, like I mentioned, there is no alternative to a tile.
